title: A family member needs support
prompt: A family member needs practical help for several months. Travel, meals, and reduced availability all have costs. You can contribute money, time, or a combination.
context: These are additional one-time costs beyond any regular family support you selected.

choices.label: Provide regular practical help
choices.text: Spend $450 on travel and supplies; commit personal time.
choices.feedback: Your help matters. Travel and time pressure still affect your own life.

choices.label: Contribute to outside help
choices.text: Spend $1,200 toward support.
choices.feedback: You protect more of your time by contributing more money.

choices.label: Coordinate shared support
choices.text: Spend $250 and work with other people on a schedule.
choices.feedback: The shared plan lowers the individual burden without eliminating it.

title: The roommate moves out
prompt: Someone sharing household costs leaves unexpectedly. Even if you live alone, this story represents losing a contribution you had counted on. You need a temporary plan.
context: This additional cost is a one-year disruption, not another permanent rent increase.

choices.label: Cover the gap while searching
choices.text: Spend $1,800 across the year.
choices.feedback: You keep housing stable, but a missing contribution consumes savings.

choices.label: Find a short-term replacement
choices.text: Spend $600 on turnover and screening; accept less privacy.
choices.feedback: The gap is smaller, with time and privacy tradeoffs.

choices.label: Borrow to cover the transition
choices.text: Add $1,800 consumer debt.
choices.feedback: Housing is maintained at the cost of an interest-bearing balance.

title: A close friend is getting married
prompt: Travel, lodging, and time off would cost $950. You want to be there, but the budget is already stretched. The friendship matters regardless of what you can afford.
context: This is a discretionary event; declining does not imply poor character.

choices.label: Attend the full event
choices.text: Spend $950.
choices.feedback: You share an important experience and reduce your financial buffer.

choices.label: Attend a smaller part
choices.text: Spend $350 and explain your limits.
choices.feedback: A clear conversation helps you participate within a tighter budget.

choices.label: Celebrate another way
choices.text: Spend $60 and make a thoughtful alternative plan.
choices.feedback: You protect cash while finding another way to show support.

title: A move becomes necessary
prompt: A change outside your control means relocating. Deposits are treated separately from spending, so these $1,500 are moving charges and nonrefundable costs only.
context: The model does not count a refundable security deposit as a permanent loss.

choices.label: Use movers
choices.feedback: You spend more to reduce the physical and scheduling burden.

choices.label: Move with help from friends
choices.text: Pay $650 for rental equipment and supplies.
choices.feedback: Help lowers the cash cost while using several people’s time.

choices.label: Finance part of the move
choices.text: Pay $400 now and add $1,100 consumer debt.
choices.feedback: The move is completed with an ongoing repayment obligation.

title: A week that stretches into a month
prompt: Unexpected appointments and household problems take more time than planned. Convenience purchases can save time, but the extra spending is outside your normal grocery budget.
context: Every option involves a tradeoff; there is no free instant recovery.

choices.label: Pay for convenience
choices.text: Spend $500 on services and prepared meals.
choices.feedback: You buy back some time at a clear cash cost.

choices.label: Handle tasks yourself
choices.text: Spend $100 on supplies and use evenings.
choices.feedback: You keep costs lower while taking on most of the workload.

choices.label: Ask for help and simplify
choices.text: Spend $200 and postpone some nonessential tasks.
choices.feedback: A smaller plan reduces pressure but leaves some things unfinished.

title: Your emergency reserve is tested
prompt: A weather-related disruption damages belongings and interrupts ordinary routines. The insurance arrangement in this fictional scenario leaves a deductible and replacement costs.
context: Insurance reduces some risks; it does not mean every loss is fully reimbursed.

choices.label: Replace essentials now
choices.text: Spend $1,400 after the covered portion.
choices.feedback: You restore the basics while using a substantial amount of cash.

choices.label: Replace only urgent items
choices.text: Spend $600 and live with the inconvenience.
choices.feedback: The smaller outlay preserves money but does not restore everything.

choices.label: Finance the essentials
choices.text: Add $1,400 consumer debt.
choices.feedback: The essentials return immediately, with a balance that carries forward.

title: Someone depends on your time
prompt: A person you care about needs reliable weekly help. You can adjust your work hours, pay for some support, or share the responsibility.
context: Reduced paid hours affect gross income; household help affects cash.

choices.label: Reduce paid work temporarily
choices.text: Lose $2,200 gross this year.
choices.feedback: Your presence matters. The smaller paycheck leaves the regular bills harder to meet.

choices.label: Pay for some additional support
choices.text: Spend $900.
choices.feedback: Support protects your work schedule while costing cash.

choices.label: Coordinate a shared plan
choices.text: Spend $350 and accept a complicated schedule.
choices.feedback: The shared effort is less expensive for you but takes coordination.

title: Your living space affects your health
prompt: A problem at home is disrupting sleep. You can pursue a formal repair process, pay for a temporary solution, or tolerate it for now.
context: This scenario assumes a route to request repairs; it does not give legal advice about tenant rights.

choices.label: Document and request repairs
choices.text: Spend $150 on temporary supplies and time documenting the issue.
choices.feedback: You create a clear record. The process still takes time and is not an instant fix.

choices.label: Pay for temporary accommodation
choices.text: Spend $900 to get a break from the situation.
choices.feedback: You protect rest at a significant financial cost.

choices.label: Keep tolerating it
choices.text: Spend no extra cash now.
choices.feedback: Avoiding the cash cost leaves an ongoing well-being problem.

title: A chance to volunteer
prompt: A project you care about needs weekend help. Participation costs travel money and time; it can also bring meaning and new connections.
context: Community contribution has value without an automatic financial return.

choices.label: Commit regularly
choices.text: Spend $300 across the year and give up several weekends.
choices.feedback: The project benefits from your work, and your personal schedule has less space.

choices.label: Take a smaller role
choices.text: Spend $100 and attend a few sessions.
choices.feedback: You contribute within a more limited commitment.

choices.label: Wait until you have capacity
choices.text: Keep your time and cash this year.
choices.feedback: A boundary protects capacity even when you wish you could do more.

title: The support you gave becomes ongoing
prompt: A family need that looked temporary will last longer. Your existing responsibilities do not disappear. You must decide what level of recurring contribution you can sustain.
context: This decision adds to any support already included in your chosen household plan.

choices.label: Contribute money each month
choices.text: Add $150/month to family support.
choices.feedback: Reliable support becomes a continuing budget obligation.

choices.label: Contribute time and a smaller amount
choices.text: Add $50/month and commit regular personal time.
choices.feedback: The cash contribution is smaller, but your time commitment is larger.

choices.label: Help locate other resources
choices.text: Spend $200 once and coordinate alternatives.
choices.feedback: You contribute coordination and a limited amount of cash. The story assumes another support arrangement is available.

title: Rest has become a necessity
prompt: You are running low on energy. A reset could involve paid activities, unpaid time away, or changing how you use evenings. There is no option that expands both time and money without a tradeoff.
context: Well-being is part of the result, not a decorative bonus.

choices.label: Take unpaid recovery time
choices.text: Lose $1,200 gross this year.
choices.feedback: Rest improves several parts of life while reducing income.

choices.label: Plan a paid break
choices.text: Spend $650.
choices.feedback: The break helps you recover without lost pay in this story, but uses savings.

choices.label: Protect low-cost evenings
choices.text: Cut social spending by $20/month and simplify commitments.
choices.feedback: A modest change is more affordable and brings a smaller improvement.

title: A milestone worth celebrating
prompt: After years of work you want to celebrate a personal milestone. You can choose a larger event, a modest gathering, or a free activity. None of these choices changes your career qualifications.
context: The point is to balance priorities, not to eliminate every enjoyable expense.

choices.label: Host the celebration you imagined
choices.text: Spend $1,200.
choices.feedback: A meaningful celebration has a real opportunity cost.

choices.label: Plan a smaller gathering
choices.text: Spend $350.
choices.feedback: You celebrate while keeping more room in the budget.

choices.label: Choose a free shared activity
choices.text: Spend no extra cash and organize the activity yourself.
choices.feedback: You preserve cash while putting in planning time.
